# dsh-memory-dba
中文功能范围说明 · 记忆操作与数据格式
File-based long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness, stored as plain files you can read, diff, and comm
e-based long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness, stored as plain files you can read, diff, and commit.
Session logs answer "what happened in this conversation". This plugin answers "what did we decide th
ree weeks ago" — across sessions, across machines, and across models.
This package is the **file-memory and retrieval plugin** of DBA. Version 0.3.0 adds its own complete
sanitized text events, recoverable stream publication, topic cards and versioned facts. The origina
l Python RWKV backend and processing pipeline remain separate; no state model is enabled by this cha
thon RWKV backend and processing pipeline remain separate; no state model is enabled by this change.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Everything lives in one directory. Copy it, put it in git, point two harness installs at the same fo
lder, or read it with `cat`. There is no database or required embedding service.
## Scope: implemented, not migrated, and not yet accepted
### 1. Implemented in this npm package
| Capability | What this package actually does |
| Three-layer file memory | `core.md`, `stream.md`, `ws/<area>.md` under one directory, plain UTF-8,

no database. `init` creates the layout; existing files are never overwritten. |
| Split prompt inje
ction | `core` is a system-prompt section (default order `-50`), snapshotted once per session. Retri
eval `hits` are runtime context (default order `300`), which the harness materializes as a trailing
user snapshot. A hit list inside the system prompt would change the head of the request and invalida

te every message behind it. |
| BM25 retrieval | BM25 (`k1=1.5`, `b=0.75`) with CJK unigrams/bigrams
. Level 1 searches `stream` text plus **workspace file names, first-line titles and explicit topic-c
ard fields**; `core.md` is injected in full and stays out of the recall corpus, so the same text can
not spend the budget twice (same rule as the Python side). Workspace bodies are not in the corpus at
all (see Retrieval). Recency reranking only reorders candidates that relevance already found, and o

nly when they overflow the byte budget. |
| Optional Ollama / bge-m3 semantic recall | Cosine hits a
bove `minScore` from a `<home>/.vec/embeddings.json` cache are appended after keyword hits without r
eordering the keyword results. Workspace entries in that cache are name-only documents, so a semanti
c hit cannot bypass level 1 and surface a body. Synchronous 1,500 ms budget (`Atomics.wait` on a wor
ker), 60 s cooldown after a failure, silent degradation to BM25. The cache is built by the CLI, not

automatically. |
| DSH session-event integration | Persists text drafts, archives completion before
publishing the stream, and recovers completed unpublished events on mount. Interrupted records remai

n inspectable without replaying them as completed turns. |
| Current stream writing | Bounded head-a
nd-tail excerpts (300/600 characters), with `[event=ID]` pointing to complete sanitized text in `eve

nts-v1`. Explicit observation labels are candidates, not automatically verified facts. |
[该节后续省略]
### 2. Exists in the original Python DBA, not migrated into this package
| Capability | Original Python DBA | In this package |
| RWKV-7 continuous session state and summary backend | `scripts/nb_rwkv.py`, `scripts/nb_rwkv_bridg
e.py`; `scripts/nb_turn.py` uses the local RWKV backend by default for session recursion, summaries,

and branch isolation. | No RWKV backend, no state interface, no summary generation. |
| Complete ev
ents and event-vector recall | Original complete events and vector recall under `.turns`. | Own comp

lete text archive under `events-v1`; no event vectors or old-archive migration. |
| Persistent outbo
x and retries | Original multi-stage pipeline. | Own durable text drafts and recoverable stream-publ

ication queue; no RWKV processing stages. |
| Message drafts and interrupted turns | Original resume

pipeline. | Text drafts persist; interrupted dialogue is not automatically resumed. |
| Controlled
`core` / `ws` writes | Dedicated `remember_core` / `remember_ws` write paths with their own checks.
| CLI `write` appends to `stream.md` only; `core.md` and `ws/*.md` are edited with ordinary file too

ls. |
| Index-maintenance loop | Chained maintenance for the keyword index, notebook vectors, and ev
ent vectors. | BM25 invalidates its corpus cache on file metadata changes; the semantic cache is reb
uilt only by a manual `index` run. |
These are real capabilities of the original Python system, not hypothetical future work. Installing
this npm package does **not** install them. The plugin does not claim parity with the Python DBA. Th
ey may coexist, but concurrent writes to the same memory directory are not coordinated; use one writ
er per shared directory.
### 3. Research not yet accepted for use in the overall DBA project
Two state interfaces were tried, and neither validates the other:
[该节后续省略]
### Legacy note
[该节后续省略]
## Limits and operating notes
Read these before relying on the plugin as shared or historical memory.
[该节后续省略]
## Why the two placements differ
The core layer changes every few days; retrieval hits change on every user turn. Both are model-visi
ble, but only one of them may sit in the system prompt.
A system-prompt section is the first message of every request, so any change to it moves the head of
the prompt: prefix caching then misses from that point on, and every message after the system promp
t — the entire conversation — is re-sent uncached. Runtime context does not have that cost. The harn
ess materializes it as a user-role snapshot appended after the conversation, so replacing it invalid
ates only the tokens that follow it, which for a per-turn block is the turn itself.
Core text is read on the first assembly of each session and replayed from that session's snapshot, s
o `core.md` edits take effect in a new session without paying a disk read on every assembly. Snapsho
ts remain until `session/disposed` and the cache therefore grows with the number and size of live se
ssion snapshots; disposal releases each one. Set `coreRefresh: 'always'` when edits must be visible
immediately inside a live session. Without a session id (diagnostics, tests, non-agent assembly), th
e plugin rereads every time and keeps only a single last-read slot.
